title: Prove one-disk cutover readiness
goal: After the facts/hardware gate, managed-build implementation, disposable activation proof and storage-rehearsal harness are terminal and reviewed, prove one-disk NixOS cutover readiness on an exclusively reserved disposable non-production target: bind the complete reviewed declarative source as a content-addressed immutable snapshot, rehearse the exact canonical LUKS2+Btrfs topology from a blank virtual disk, restore independently sourced off-host backup material, reconstruct and boot a fresh system only from that snapshot, prove offline recovery, and finish with a reviewed evidence-complete cutover plan whose actual production device remains deliberately unbound for a later separately authorized destructive order.

approval.note: Runtime/block-device mutation is authorized only inside the exclusively reserved disposable service.heim-pc-nixos-storage-rehearsal-sandbox and only after T001, T002, T004 and T005 are terminal and reviewed. The narrow T005 harness paths are externally reserved while the rehearsal is bound, while every declarative reconstruction/build input is consumed from a content-addressed immutable whole-source snapshot materialized from the exact reviewed Heim-PC Git revision inside the exclusive sandbox. After snapshot binding, use of the mutable Heim-PC checkout, a branch, a re-resolved lock or an unpinned remote source fails closed. The productive Heim-PC block devices, EFI, Secure-Boot, firmware, boot state and OS remain outside this authority.

acceptance.assertion: Before any block-device/runtime effect, the run is bound to the exact terminal T005 source revision and independent review evidence, and holds external reservations for nixos/rehearsal, scripts/nixos_storage_rehearsal.py and tests/test_nixos_storage_rehearsal.py for the whole rehearsal; any dirty state, revision drift, lease loss or missing review fails closed.

Before any block-device or boot effect, a single exact reviewed Heim-PC Git revision selected after T001, T002, T004 and T005 are terminal is materialized inside the exclusive storage-rehearsal sandbox as a content-addressed immutable whole-source snapshot. Evidence binds Git commit and tree identity, snapshot digest, Control Release Set and lock/input identity. All flake/lock, host/user modules, storage declarations, facts outputs, managed-deployment configuration and other reconstruction inputs are read only from this snapshot; after binding, any fallback to /home/alex/repos/heim-pc, a branch, a mutable lock or an unpinned remote source fails closed before effect.

Before sgdisk, wipefs, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs or boot mutation, the run holds the exclusive service.heim-pc-nixos-storage-rehearsal-sandbox claim and fresh independent evidence proves the target is a blank disposable virtual disk whose backing is not the productive Heim-PC root/system disk, not any mounted production filesystem and not production EFI/firmware state; ambiguity fails closed before effect.

Starting from the independently proven blank disposable virtual disk and the hash-bound immutable declarative source snapshot, the exact production-target topology GPT + EFI System Partition + recovery/boot-recovery surface + LUKS2 + Btrfs with @root, @nix, @persist, @home, @data and @containers is created, LUKS unlock is proven, every Btrfs subvolume is mounted correctly, the resulting disposable system actually boots, and independent readback proves the expected topology; the earlier LUKS+ext4 VM proof is not substituted for this gate.

Fresh read-only inventory classifies every migration-relevant non-reproducible data class separately from caches and rebuildable state; current scoped backup success is not treated as proof of complete cutover coverage.

Every critical migration data class is covered by sufficient physically/logically independent off-host storage and a staged realistic restore into the disposable rehearsal sandbox proves representative usable content; a capacity-constrained, production-disk-backed or non-independently-restorable backup target cannot satisfy this gate.

A fresh disposable system is reconstructed exclusively from the hash-bound immutable reviewed declarative source snapshot plus independently restored non-reproducible data, demonstrating that neither mutable checkout state, hidden production-host state nor the original system disk is required for recovery. The resulting boot/readback evidence binds the reconstructed system to the same source snapshot and approved closure identity.

Independent bootable recovery media plus the required offline host/control closure, hash-bound source snapshot, lock/trust roots and LUKS/recovery material are verified without Grabowski, Bureau, network or the production system SSD.

The cutover plan defines the exact later device-binding procedure and required fresh evidence for model, serial number, mounts, root backing, health and recovery readiness, but deliberately leaves the actual production block-device identity unbound until a separate destructive cutover order authorizes it; historical WD_BLACK SN850X/nvme0n1 evidence is orientation only.

The terminal artifact is a reviewed evidence object/plan binding the approved activation-proof evidence, immutable declarative source-snapshot digest, exact target topology, point of no return, rollback/reconstruction procedure, mandatory post-boot readback and all prerequisite backup/recovery evidence, while containing no current authorization or production block-device binding for the real cutover.

Although destructive commands are required inside the exclusive disposable sandbox, this task terminates before sgdisk, wipefs, cryptsetup luksFormat, mkfs, real EFI-partition mutation, Secure-Boot key mutation, firmware write, productive nixos-install, productive switch or reboot into a new production OS on the Heim-PC; such effects require a later explicit destructive-action order bound to fresh production-device and recovery evidence.

Exact source-snapshot, target-preflight, VM/storage topology, boot/readback, backup restore, fresh reconstruction, offline recovery and final-plan evidence are independently reviewed before T003 is considered terminal.

metadata.historical_device_reference_not_authorit: WD_BLACK SN850X 2TB / historical nvme0n1 orientation only; actual production device identity is intentionally unbound in this task
